title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A refactoring offered inside a comment
summary: Add names to call arguments read the cursor line one line at a time, so the body of a KDoc or of a raw string passed for code.

highlights.title: Prose that looked like a call
highlights.description: A KDoc line such as taller (late reflow, slow assets) has the exact shape of a call with two arguments. On a real project, 642 such sites were read out of comments and strings.

highlights.title: Read from the code, not from the text
highlights.description: Candidates come from a copy of the line with comments and string contents blanked out. A call after a block comment on the same line, or inside a string template, is still real code and still gets the action.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Add names to call arguments is no longer offered on the body of a KDoc, a block comment or a raw string.
A call sitting after a comment on the same line, or inside a string template, keeps the action.
The blanked copy of the file is computed once per version, so the lightbulb stays free after the first request.
